questions.stem: A newborn is born with lower extremity paralysis, an absent sacrum, and impaired bladder and bowel control. On examination, there is a clear demarcation between the normal and affected spinal regions. What is the most likely diagnosis for this infant's condition, and what is the underlying pathophysiology?

options.label: A
options.text: Caudal regression syndrome; Abnormal development of the lower spinal cord and vertebral structures.

options.label: B
options.text: Spina bifida occulta; A neural tube defect resulting in a bony spinal defect

options.label: C
options.text: Neurofibromatosis type 1; A genetic disorder causing neurofibromas and spinal abnormalities.
